comment: Feeds (SPEC §6.6a, §14.1, §18.3): the owner-rooted event channel. THE FIXTURE IS THE AUTHORITY for the shapes that must agree byte-for-byte across the TypeScript SDK, the Rust SDK, the adapter, and the platform: the subject grammar (exactly four tokens, owner nkey then a single topic token), the feed emit payload ({topic, kind, data} — NOT the {domain, event_type, data} of a domain emit), the state-feed KV key ({agent_id}.{topic}), and the current-value lookup on mesh.feed.get ({agent, topic} in, {found, envelope} out). Divergences here are one-byte ones: a dot that splits a topic, an owner token in the wrong position, a payload keyed domain instead of topic. Tests iterate the case arrays; a new row must run without touching any test.

identities.comment: A published test-vector user nkey (public half only; no case here signs).

subjects.comment: The grammar: mesh.feed.{owner nkey}.{topic}, exactly four tokens; the topic is ONE token of [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}. The lookup subject mesh.feed.get has three tokens and is therefore never a feed. Builders MUST refuse invalid topics rather than emit a subject that the transport grant (mesh.feed.<own key>.*) would reject or that would smuggle extra tokens.

payload.comment: A feed publish is an ordinary emit envelope (type 'emit', §6.6 — no new envelope fields) whose payload is {topic, kind, data}. NOT {domain, event_type, data}: a feed topic is a single token and must never be split on dots the way a domain-event topic is. 'kind' is 'state' or 'stream' (§6.6a), carried in-band so the platform and subscribers learn it from traffic without a manifest read.

shape_cases.comment: state feed payload, canonical member set

state_binding.comment: §18.3: the platform records the LATEST emit envelope per feed under KV key {agent_id}.{topic}, and serves it over request-reply on mesh.feed.get. The lookup request payload is {agent, topic}; the response payload is {found: true, envelope: <the stored emit envelope>} or {found: false, envelope: null}. Subscribe-before-snapshot (§9.6) is the CALLER's obligation and is behavioural, not byte-pinnable — it is asserted in each SDK's own tests, not here.

lookup_request_cases.comment: the request names the feed, nothing else

lookup_response_members.found: boolean — whether the feed has ever published
lookup_response_members.envelope: the stored emit envelope when found is true; null when false

separation.comment: Feed deliveries are AMBIENT: they route to the event handler (onEvent), never to the mail path, never into inbox or waiting counts, and are never sealed (§6.6 — events are open broadcast; content that requires sealing travels in a request). Behavioural; asserted per implementation.
